strengths: The paper presents a coherent combination of dense future RGB/depth supervision and uncertainty-guided RL post-training. Using one world-modeling component for both representation learning and intrinsic reward is conceptually appealing.
The NAVSIM v2 result is strong: ExploreVLA reports an EPDMS of 88.8, 2.7 points above the listed prior best, with favorable performance across several submetrics despite using only a front camera.

The dense-supervision ablation is useful: RGB and depth generation independently improve PDMS, and their combination raises it from 86.2 to 88.5, supporting the claim that the auxiliary objectives benefit planning.
The evaluation includes NAVSIM v1/v2, two nuScenes protocols, component ablations, and qualitative examples. The architecture and two-stage training pipeline are generally presented clearly.
weaknesses: The evidence for the main novelty—uncertainty-driven exploration—is weak. PDMS-only GRPO improves PDMS from 88.50 to 90.19, while adding the image reward yields only 90.36; image reward alone gives 88.53. Thus nearly all Stage-2 improvement comes from optimizing PDMS, and the paper provides no seeds, uncertainty estimates, or significance analysis showing that the 0.17-point gain is reliable.

The manuscript does not establish that token predictive entropy measures epistemic novelty or distance from the expert distribution. Entropy can reflect aleatoric visual ambiguity, tokenizer behavior, or scene complexity unrelated to the sampled action. Figure 3 supplies neither a correlation coefficient nor a controlled OOD evaluation, and its single qualitative example is insufficient. Comparisons against trajectory-distance bonuses, random bonuses, ensembles, or calibrated uncertainty estimators are missing.

Critical GRPO details are underspecified. The policy is described as a continuous MLP trajectory head, but the paper never defines its stochastic distribution, how candidate trajectories are sampled, or how their log probabilities and KL terms are computed. It is also unclear how a sampled continuous trajectory conditions image generation. These omissions make the central optimization procedure difficult to assess or reproduce.

Equation 5 is at best ambiguous and apparently does not compute categorical entropy correctly: it sums one p_j log p_j term per generated position rather than summing over all 8,192 codebook probabilities at every position. The normalization function f in Equation 6 is also unspecified. Both directly determine the proposed reward.

The headline NAVSIM v1 score of 93.7 uses best-of-six inference, whereas the ordinary prediction scores 90.4 and trails several listed methods. The manuscript does not explain how the six candidates are selected at test time, whether selection requires privileged PDMS information, or the added compute. Consequently, the claimed deployable state of the art is not fully substantiated, although the v2 result remains encouraging.

There is no direct evaluation of the claimed outcome—broader behavioral repertoire and improved OOD generalization. The experiments report aggregate benchmark scores but not trajectory diversity, coverage of novel strategies, performance under distribution shifts, or long-tail breakdowns. The non-reactive NAVSIM setting also cannot demonstrate genuine environment interaction or safe exploration.

Reproducibility and practical evidence are incomplete: no code link is actually supplied, loss weights and several decoding/reward details are absent, results lack multi-seed variation, and image-generation quality is only shown qualitatively. Runtime, parameter count, and test-time cost are not reported. The limitations discussion omits these central issues and the safety risks of rewarding uncertainty.

strengths: The paper addresses an important computer-vision problem: improving end-to-end autonomous-driving policies beyond behavior cloning while enriching their visual and geometric representations.

Joint future RGB/depth generation is a sensible auxiliary objective. The NAVSIM ablation reports consistent gains over trajectory-only training: PDMS increases from 86.2 to 87.9 with RGB, 87.8 with depth, and 88.5 with both.
The reported NAVSIM results are strong, including 88.8 EPDMS on v2. The method uses only a front-facing camera yet compares favorably with several multi-camera or LiDAR systems.

The evaluation covers NAVSIM v1/v2 and nuScenes, includes component ablations, and provides qualitative trajectory and generation examples. The manuscript is generally organized clearly and situates the approach among recent VLA and world-model methods.
weaknesses: The central RL mechanism is not specified well enough to establish technical soundness or reproducibility. Trajectories come from a continuous MLP head, but the paper never defines a stochastic action distribution, how the G trajectories are sampled, or how their policy likelihoods are obtained. The presented GRPO description stops at normalized advantages and omits the actual clipped policy objective, old-policy ratios, reference policy, and KL term, despite later listing GRPO hyperparameters.

It is unclear how the world model produces counterfactual futures conditioned on each sampled trajectory. Training images are logged futures associated with expert actions, while arbitrary sampled actions have no corresponding visual targets. The architecture and attention/factorization description does not clearly ensure causal action-conditioned generation. Consequently, high uncertainty may reflect unsupported counterfactual inputs or model error rather than meaningful behavioral novelty.

The key assumption that image-token entropy measures distance from the expert distribution is asserted rather than demonstrated. Predictive entropy can also arise from aleatoric scene ambiguity, visual complexity, poor calibration, or tokenizer errors. Figure 3 supplies only a small scatter plot without sample count, correlation statistics, calibration/OOD tests, or comparisons with established novelty estimators. Equation 5 is also ambiguous or incorrect as written: categorical entropy should sum over all codebook probabilities at every token position, whereas the displayed expression appears to use only one probability per position.

Evidence for the proposed exploration bonus is very weak. Adding it to PDMS-based GRPO improves PDMS only from 90.19 to 90.36, while the image reward alone changes 88.50 to 88.53. No repeated runs, error bars, statistical tests, or results on held-out distribution shifts are supplied, so these small differences do not support claims of discovering diverse strategies or improving generalization beyond expert demonstrations.

The headline NAVSIM-v1 result of 93.7 relies on best-of-six selection. The ordinary single-output score is 90.4, below several reported baselines, and the paper does not adequately describe the selection mechanism, its computational cost, or a controlled comparison against applying the same sampling budget to all methods. Calling NAVSIM's non-reactive pseudo-simulation metrics “closed-loop” is also misleading.

Dense world modeling is evaluated only indirectly through planning scores and a qualitative montage. There are no RGB-generation, depth-estimation, temporal-consistency, or action-controllability metrics, making it impossible to determine whether the learned component is a credible world model rather than merely an auxiliary reconstruction task. Depth supervision itself comes from pseudo-labels generated by Metric3D, but the impact of their errors is not analyzed.

The nuScenes evidence does not demonstrate the claimed generalization of the complete method: Stage 2 is not applied, ExploreVLA has worse average L2 error than multiple VLA baselines under ST-P3, UniAD-protocol collision results are missing, and no uncertainty/exploration analysis is reported there.

Important reproducibility details remain absent, including the exact normalization function f, trajectory-sampling procedure, best-of-N ranking rule, complete loss weights, update schedule, evaluation variance, and training sample counts. The promised code link is blank. Limitations discuss camera coverage but omit the more consequential issues of offline counterfactual validity, uncertainty calibration, benchmark leakage/overfitting, and the safety implications of rewarding model uncertainty. Overall, the promising benchmark numbers and auxiliary-supervision result are insufficient to validate the paper's main exploration contribution.

strengths: The paper presents a timely and original combination of dense future-scene modeling and uncertainty-guided reinforcement learning for end-to-end autonomous driving. Using the same world model both for RGB/depth supervision and as a novelty signal is conceptually appealing.

The empirical results are strong. ExploreVLA reaches 93.7 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 with best-of-six selection and 88.8 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2, with the latter exceeding the reported prior best by 2.7 points while using only a front-view camera.

The dense-supervision ablation is convincing: RGB and depth generation independently improve PDMS from 86.2 to 87.9 and 87.8, respectively, and their combination reaches 88.5, supporting the claim that appearance and geometry provide complementary training signals.

The reward ablation separates standard PDMS-based RL from the proposed exploration bonus. The complete reward gives the best result, and the qualitative examples illustrate corrections of collision, pedestrian-proximity, and stop-sign failures after RL post-training.

The method is evaluated on both NAVSIM and nuScenes, includes comparisons under two nuScenes protocols, and provides useful implementation details, qualitative world-model outputs, and a limitations section. The paper is generally clear and well organized.
weaknesses: The flagship exploration contribution receives only limited quantitative support. Adding the image uncertainty bonus to PDMS-based GRPO improves PDMS from 90.19 to 90.36, without multiple seeds, confidence intervals, or significance analysis. Most of the Stage-2 gain comes from the ordinary PDMS reward rather than the proposed novelty term.

The assertion that token entropy measures distance from the entire expert training distribution is not established. Entropy can also reflect aleatoric scene ambiguity, tokenizer frequency, visual complexity, or poor calibration. Figure 3 provides a small qualitative example and an unlabeled scatter plot, but no OOD-detection metrics, calibration study, correlation coefficient, or comparison with alternative novelty estimators.

Important mechanics are underspecified. The paper does not clearly explain how a sampled continuous trajectory conditions future-image generation, how the MLP trajectory head defines a distribution from which the G rollouts are sampled, or the actual clipped GRPO objective used to update that head. Equation 5 also appears notationally incomplete because entropy should sum over codebook entries for every generated position, rather than using one probability per image-token position.

There is no quantitative evaluation of world-model quality, despite image prediction being central to both supervision and reward. Metrics for RGB/depth prediction, action controllability, uncertainty calibration, and comparisons against trajectory-distance, ensemble, or latent-feature novelty rewards would materially strengthen the scientific case. Sensitivity analyses for the safety threshold and exploration weight are also absent.

NAVSIM is a non-reactive pseudo-simulation benchmark, so its scores do not demonstrate genuine environment interaction or closed-loop exploration under action-induced state transitions. The language about trial-and-error exploration and closed-loop behavior should therefore be qualified, ideally with reactive simulation or targeted OOD/long-tail evaluation.

The state-of-the-art NAVSIM v1 result relies on best-of-six selection and exceeds the strongest listed results by a small margin whose variability is unknown. On nuScenes, where Stage 2 is not applied, L2 accuracy is mixed and some collision results under the UniAD protocol are missing. Runtime, parameter count, and inference cost are likewise unreported despite the added image-generation machinery.
